body:
CANONICAL: Greg's continuous-work and handoff direction (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-17; relayed by Engram::Advisor, mailbox-74a6af16). These are Greg's words or the Advisor's restatement of them. They carry no higher authority than his current word, and grant no commit, push, install, restart or authority widening.

#1577 (2026-10-17, Advisor's restatement): work proceeds continuously; avoid idle capacity. A quiet period is acceptable only while another project's active full gate needs it. Every recovered lane has a distinct code, test, review or design action with a NAMED RELEASE CONDITION, or a precise external blocker. Separate worktrees for independent items; Sol 6.1 primarily for coding. No overlapping heavy gates. Don't leave work waiting merely for a coordinator wake. Report active and held lanes, with the next action per lane, at gate boundaries.

#1578: work must not stop until Greg asks for status (proof: the 08:34-15:36Z stall). A P1 host handoff fix (TermAl w-d9f93ea08fd2, a host-local ledger; Engram w-42326 PARKED as not needed). Until it lands: an explicit watchdog over Engram and TermAl gates and carriers.
#1583: classify every idle lane as (a) waiting on a resource window, (b) external decision or (c) dispatchable, wake every (c) at once, and report the active count. Acceptance case on w-d9f9: a status observation must not be needed for the scan to happen.

#1580, Greg VERBATIM: "Pytania do mnie mogą być w fazie projektowej. Nie powinni nigdy blokować pracy." Record each question with its recommended default and continue reversible work on the default where authority permits. An explicit Greg PAUSE or STOP on an item (for example w-46f2, w-e775) is NOT a question and still holds: check item notes before dispatch.

#1592 (2026-10-17 17:44Z, Advisor's restatement): do not spend more capacity attributing the 20 s admission stall with small synthetic benchmarks. Greg directly observes seconds of 100% NVMe and host unresponsiveness. Treat HOST DISK SATURATION as a real operating condition: keep the concrete typed-busy fix (w-b64c), prioritize production-size or host telemetry only when it informs a fix, and SCHEDULE AND BACKPRESSURE heavy work so it doesn't overlap destructively. Continue independent correctness work. Never present a quiet-slot benchmark as evidence that the incident is absent.

HOW ENGRAM::FABLE APPLIES IT:
- Watchdog: a cron tick every 10 min in session-5135 (re-create it after a restart or compaction): unread mail, terminal unrelayed runs, overdue TermAl promises, idle lanes with a met release condition, claim expiry, free disk. Every handoff names its successor and a deadline.
- Backpressure (proposed to Fable2 17:45Z): in shared windows at most 3 concurrent cargo or npm builds across both projects, cold compiles one at a time, at most 2 per project, staggered; full gates strictly serial.
- Greg questions with defaults: w-b447 (a) loaded run; w-8caf default B; w-15b4 durability (1) keep the close checkpoint; WSL #1514 (criteria amended to verifiable evidence). Reserved acts still need Greg's own word: store-format change or migration, authority widening, TermAl restarts, deploy, global configuration.

REMOTE IS FIRST-CLASS (Greg's direct direction, relayed by Advisor #1624, message 75a29bd8, 2026-10-17 20:40Z): "remote must become a first-class citizen. It supersedes the previous endpoint-only/operator-relay target for this work. Two required workstreams: (1) remote mailbox that supports normal cross-host coordination; (2) Engram synchronization between hosts. TermAl Fable2 and both TermAl architects were directed to create/joint-design the host side. ... record this as a current Greg direction, unpark only the necessary portable/sync design scope, and join the joint design for the Engram sync boundary, authority, conflicts, recovery and staged rollout. No code before the shared design has been reviewed and decomposed."
EFFECT: the 2026-10-02 portable-handoff STOP (memory rules-greg-standing-direction, STOPPED) is LIFTED FOR DESIGN ONLY, for the scope Engram host-to-host sync needs: w-e775b8a167af (portable V9) and the Git task-sync exchange design (w-42885a9ab4f4, w-65fb79ead0c3). Still not allowed until the shared design is reviewed and decomposed: implementation, code task activation, or new sync landings. Already-frozen git-sync E1 (w-0ba5) continues. The #920 "no distributed work" hold is superseded for this workstream. Engram design lead: SyncArchitect (11355), with Architect1 (9550); joint with TermAl's Fable2 and its two architects.

Q6 DECIDED + ENGRAM DECENTRALIZED (Greg via Advisor, message d9cce9a0, 2026-10-17 21:02Z): "Greg accepted Q6 YES: disconnected hosts may duplicate task work. He clarifies Engram is decentralized: code and task status are reconciled during ordinary Git merge. TermAl, separately, enables strict centralization for control/mailboxes. Revise the Engram sync design accordingly: Git merge/import is the cross-host task-status reconciliation mechanism; no attempt to centralize Engram claims/runtime or use TermAl mailbox as task state. Coordinate exact wording with Fable2/architects before slices." Also (TermAl Advisor #1070): mailbox storage lives only at its one home host, with no mirroring; the sender outbox is retry-only.

GENUINELY DISTRIBUTED, HOST-NEUTRAL (Greg via Advisor #1627, message 558cc26c, 21:11Z): "Greg plans to add Linux and a second Windows host after MacBookPro and wants the system genuinely distributed. Keep Engram's decentralized Git push/fetch/merge/import design host-neutral from the first pilot; identify the enrollment/origin configuration and a minimal 3+ host Git-only pilot path, without changing claims/runtime authority. Coordinate terminology with central-TermAl hub-and-spoke." LATER CLUSTER SCHEDULER (#1628, message 557681e2, 21:12Z): after the remote mailbox, Git Engram sync and host onboarding, the system may organise and assign work by capabilities and capacity; Engram stays decentralized and Git-merged. This is a separate design-after-foundations item, w-d180e311c03a (deferred), with no widening of the current sync implementation and no change to authority gates.

CODE NOW (Greg via Advisor #1629, 21:16Z: "Ok. To kodujemy."): start coding the remote foundations; Engram's priority is host-neutral git-only task sync, in parallel with TermAl's central mailbox. A PAUSE at #1630 (21:20Z) was RETRACTED at #1632 (21:21Z), Greg verbatim: "Nie. Potrzebujemy mailbox i sync engram. Bez tego będzie dużo błędów. Remote foundation to jest to co potrzebujemy teraz." RESUME the Engram sync implementation, including E1 and the decomposed slices; only the cluster scheduler (w-d180) stays deferred.

STOP: AUTOMATIC FETCH DEFERRED (Greg via Advisor #1639, message e418092b, 2026-10-17 22:18Z), verbatim: "Nie nie. Nie róbcie tego. Nie teraz. Po prostu git fetch." Do not start or schedule w-8538455dd83d's automatic-fetch bounded receiver or its six slices (all blocked). For the remote pilot: ordinary explicit, authorized `git fetch` followed by the planned Engram import/reconciliation. Automatic fetch and its enforced limits are future work. E2 (w-5cf7) no longer waits on w-8538; its fetch is explicit git fetch through S0's bounded runner.

FIXTURE OPT-IN (Greg via Advisor #1642, message 2e38efd4, 2026-10-17 22:46Z), verbatim "tak", answering whether agents may enable task-sync opt-in on throwaway test stores under the repository's ignored target/ folder to rehearse multi-host Git sync on one machine. Scope: only throwaway stores under target/, solely for single-machine multi-host rehearsal; NEVER a live store or any path outside target/. The opt-in --user-instruction must quote this.

NARROW PILOT (Greg via Advisor #1645, message 3cc7f42a, 2026-10-17 22:55Z): the current pilot must NOT wait for model A, automatic convergence or a store migration; "Po prostu git fetch." Define and run the minimum useful cross-host pilot with ordinary explicit git fetch plus import: preserve work text, make conflicts and refusals visible, and have a human merger resolve divergence. Model A is later work.
